text: In the book's distance-free definition, a map f: X → Y between topological spaces is continuous if and only if:
choices: the image f(U) of every open set U ⊆ X is open in Y
the preimage f⁻¹(V) of every open set V ⊆ Y is open in X
the image of every compact subset of X is compact in Y
f maps every Cauchy sequence to a Cauchy sequence
explanation: The topological definition is that f⁻¹(V) is open in X for every open V ⊆ Y (equivalently, preimages of closed sets are closed), generalizing the ε-δ definition. Requiring images of open sets to be open defines an open map, not a continuous one; preserving compactness is a consequence of continuity, not its definition.
